claim: Legionella pneumophila delivers more than 330 effectors into host cells by its Dot/Icm secretion system.
source: The intracellular pathogen Legionella pneumophila delivers more than 330 effectors into host cells by its Dot/Icm secretion system.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about L. pneumophila.

claim: The LCV is associated with mitochondria.
source: It has long been documented that the LCV is associated with mitochondria and a number of Dot/Icm effectors have been shown to target to this organelle.
evidence: This is stated as a documented fact in the abstract.

claim: Ceg3 (Lpg0080) is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase.
source: Here, we found that the Dot/Icm substrate Ceg3 (Lpg0080) is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that localizes to the mitochondria in host cells where it attacks ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation, and blunts their ADP/ATP exchange activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ceg3 localizes to the mitochondria in host cells.
source: Here, we found that the Dot/Icm substrate Ceg3 (Lpg0080) is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that localizes to the mitochondria in host cells where it attacks ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation, and blunts their ADP/ATP exchange activity.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining (Figure 1C), immunogold labeling (Figure 1D), and cell fractionation experiments (Figure 1E-F).

claim: Ceg3 attacks ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation.
source: Here, we found that the Dot/Icm substrate Ceg3 (Lpg0080) is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that localizes to the mitochondria in host cells where it attacks ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation, and blunts their ADP/ATP exchange activity.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data (Figure 3B) and immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 3A).

claim: Ceg3 blunts ADP/ATP exchange activity of ADP/ATP translocases.
source: Here, we found that the Dot/Icm substrate Ceg3 (Lpg0080) is a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase that localizes to the mitochondria in host cells where it attacks ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation, and blunts their ADP/ATP exchange activity.
evidence: This is supported by ADP/ATP exchange rate measurements shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: The modification by Ceg3 occurs on the second arginine residue in the -RRRMMM- element.
source: The modification occurs on the second arginine residue in the -RRRMMM- element, which is conserved among all known ADP/ATP carriers from different organisms.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry analysis (Figure 3B) and mutagenesis studies (Figure 3D).

claim: The -RRRMMM- element is conserved among all known ADP/ATP carriers from different organisms.
source: The modification occurs on the second arginine residue in the -RRRMMM- element, which is conserved among all known ADP/ATP carriers from different organisms.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: L. pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease.
source: Legionella pneumophila, a Gram-negative intracellular bacterial pathogen, is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: L. pneumophila exists ubiquitously in the environment as a parasite of freshwater amoebae.
source: This bacterium exists ubiquitously in the environment as a parasite of freshwater amoebae (Richards et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Richards et al., 2013.

claim: Infection of humans occurs when susceptible individuals inhale aerosol contaminated by bacteria.
source: Infection of humans occurs when susceptible individuals inhale aerosol contaminated by bacteria and introduce the pathogen to the lungs where it is phagocytosed by alveolar macrophages.
evidence: This is established knowledge about L. pneumophila infection.

claim: Engulfed L. pneumophila bacteria survive and replicate in macrophages.
source: Instead of being digested, engulfed bacteria survive and replicate in macrophages, leading to tissue damage and strong inflammatory responses, and the development of disease symptoms (Newton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Newton et al., 2010.

claim: The biogenesis of the LCV requires the Dot/Icm system.
source: The biogenesis of the LCV requires the Dot/Icm system, which is arguably the most important pathogenic factor of L. pneumophila (Hubber and Roy, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hubber and Roy, 2010.

claim: Mutations in any component gene essential for the function of the Dot/Icm transporter result in a complete loss of virulence on all hosts.
source: Mutations in any component gene essential for the function of the Dot/Icm transporter result in a complete loss of virulence on all hosts.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Dot/Icm system.

claim: The Dot/Icm machine injects more than 330 virulence factors known as effectors into host cells.
source: This multicomponent machine injects more than 330 virulence factors known as effectors into host cells to construct the LCV by manipulating diverse cellular processes, including vesicle trafficking, autophagy, lipid metabolism, and cytoskeleton structure via distinct biochemical activities (Qiu and Luo, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Qiu and Luo, 2017.

claim: ADP-ribosylation is one of the first identified PTMs utilized by toxins from bacterial pathogens.
source: Among these, ADP-ribosylation is one of the first identified PTMs utilized by toxins from bacterial pathogens (Aravind et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Aravind et al., 2015.

claim: ADP-ribosylation is catalyzed by ADP-ribosyltransferases (ARTs) that transfer the ADP-ribose moiety from NAD to target substrates.
source: this modification is catalyzed by ADP-ribosyltransferases (ARTs) that transfer the ADP-ribose moiety from nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) to target substrates via an N-, O-, or S-glycosidic linkage (Cohen and Chang, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cohen and Chang, 2018.

claim: The diphtheria toxin inhibits host protein synthesis by modifying elongation factor 2 (EF2).
source: Some of the best studied examples include the inhibition of host protein synthesis by the diphtheria toxin that modifies elongation factor 2 (EF2) (Honjo et al., 1968)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Honjo et al., 1968.

claim: The cholera toxin interferes with host second messenger cAMP production by ADP-ribosylating the Gαs subunit of adenylate cyclase.
source: the interference of the host second messenger cAMP production by the cholera toxin, which ADP-ribosylates the Gαs subunit of the adenylate cyclase and locks the enzyme in an active form (Cassel and Pfeuffer, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cassel and Pfeuffer, 1978.

claim: The type III effector ExoS of Pseudomonas aeruginosa targets multiple cellular proteins, including Ras.
source: For example, the type III effector ExoS of Pseudomonas aeruginosa targets multiple cellular proteins, including Ras, the modification of which leads to the inhibition of ROS production by neutrophils (Vareechon et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Vareechon et al., 2017.

claim: The T3SS effector SopF from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium attacks the ATP6V0C subunit of v-ATPase by ADP-ribosylation.
source: Recently, Xu et al., 2019 found that the T3SS effector SopF from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium attacks the ATP6V0C subunit of v-ATPase by ADP-ribosylation, thus blocking the recruitment of ATG16L1 to suppress autophagy (Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2019.

claim: CteC from Chromobacterium violaceum specifically modifies ubiquitin on Thr66 to disrupt host ubiquitin signaling.
source: One such example is CteC from Chromobacterium violaceum, which specifically modifies ubiquitin on Thr66 with a cryptic mART motif to disrupt host ubiquitin signaling (Yan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Yan et al., 2020.

claim: The effector Lpg0181 inactivates the glutamate dehydrogenase in host cells using an mART activity.
source: The effector Lpg0181 was found to inactivate the glutamate dehydrogenase in host cells using an mART activity (Black et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Black et al., 2021.

claim: Members of the SidE effector family catalyze ubiquitination of multiple host proteins by first activating ubiquitin via ADP-ribosylation on Arg42.
source: Members of the SidE effector family catalyze ubiquitination of multiple host proteins by first activating ubiquitin via ADP-ribosylation on Arg42 with an mART activity (Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Qiu et al., 2016.

claim: Ceg3 was first identified as a Dot/Icm substrate by virtue of being coregulated with known effector genes.
source: Ceg3 was first identified as a Dot/Icm substrate by virtue of being coregulated with known effector genes (Zusman et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zusman et al., 2007.

claim: Ceg3 kills the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae upon ectopic expression.
source: and was later shown to kill the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae upon ectopic expression (Urbanus et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Urbanus et al., 2016.

claim: The putative mART motif is critical for Ceg3's yeast toxicity.
source: Compared to wild-type protein that severely inhibited yeast growth, Ceg3E/A has completely lost the toxicity (Figure 1B). These results suggest that the putative mART motif is critical for the activity of Ceg3.
evidence: This is supported by yeast toxicity assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ceg3 colocalizes extensively with a mitochondrial marker with a Pearson's correlation coefficient value of 0.87.
source: Further experiments using a mitotracker reagent revealed that Ceg3 colocalizes extensively with this mitochondrial marker with a Pearson's correlation coefficient value of 0.87 (Figure 1C), suggesting that Ceg3 localizes to the mitochondria.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Flag-Ceg3 co-fractionated with PDHA1, a mitochondrial protein.
source: Flag-Ceg3 co-fractionated with the subunit α1 of pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 (PDHA1), which is an established mitochondrial protein (Børglum et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by cell fractionation data shown in Figure 1E and a citation to Børglum et al., 1997.

claim: Ceg3 is targeted to mitochondria once being injected into host cells.
source: Finally, we detected Ceg3 in mitochondrial fractions of cells infected with a wild-type L. pneumophila strain overexpressing Flag-tagged Ceg3 but not with a mutant defective in the Dot/Icm transporter (Figure 1F), suggesting that Ceg3 is targeted to mitochondria once being injected into host cells.
evidence: This is supported by infection and fractionation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ceg3 is an integral mitochondrial membrane protein.
source: In contrast, HA-Ceg3 was only detected in the pellet fraction together with the mitochondrial import receptor subunit TOM20 homolog (Tom20) and the voltage-dependent anion-selective channel protein 1 (VDAC1), two integral mitochondrial membrane proteins (Burri et al., 2006; Hiller et al., 2008). Thus, Ceg3 is not peripherally associated with mitochondrial membranes.
evidence: This is supported by carbonate extraction data shown in Figure 1G and citations to Burri et al., 2006 and Hiller et al., 2008.

claim: Ceg3 induces ADP-ribosylation of host proteins of approximately 25 kDa.
source: Signals representing proteins of slightly larger than 25 kDa were detected in lysates of cells expressing Ceg3 but not in samples expressing Ceg3E/A (Figure 2A, left and middle panels).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: ADP/ATP translocases (ANTs) are among the top proteins identified by mass spectrometry in Ceg3-modified samples.
source: Among the top 10 proteins with the most hits, with the exception of keratin, a common contaminant in mass spectrometric samples, 4 were assigned as ADP/ATP translocases (ANTs) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data referenced in Supplementary file 1.

claim: GFP-Ceg3 binds to Flag-ANT1.
source: We confirmed ANT proteins as substrates of Ceg3 by transfecting mammalian cells to express GFP-Ceg3 and Flag-ANT1, which is one isoform of ADP/ATP translocases, and examined their interactions by IP. Precipitates obtained by beads coated with the Flag antibody contained GFP-Ceg3 (Figure 2D), indicating the binding between these two proteins.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: RFP-Ceg3 colocalizes extensively with GFP-ANT1, with a Pearson's correlation coefficient value of 0.87.
source: Consistent with these results, fluorescence signals of RFP-Ceg3 colocalize extensively with those of GFP-ANT1, with a Pearson's correlation coefficient value of 0.87 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Human cells express four ADP/ATP translocase isoforms.
source: Human cells express four ADP/ATP translocase isoforms, each was identified in our mass spectrometric analysis (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and established knowledge.

claim: ANTs are essential for transferring ADP and ATP across the mitochondrial inner membranes.
source: ANTs are essential for transferring ADP and ATP across the mitochondrial inner membranes (Klingenberg, 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Klingenberg, 2008.

claim: Ceg3 modifies all four ANT isoforms by ADP-ribosylation.
source: Detection using the ADP-ribose probe revealed that each of the ANTs was modified by Ceg3 but not the mutant Ceg3E/A (Figure 3A). These results demonstrate that Ceg3 modifies these ADP/ATP translocases by ADP-ribosylation.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ceg3 modifies ANT1 by mono-ADP-ribosylation on residue Arg236.
source: MS/MS spectra showed that the modification mapped to residue Arg236, and the modified peptide produced several fragmented ions with m/z of 136.1, 250.1, 348.1, and 428.0 which are adenine, adenosine, adenosine monophosphate (AMP), and adenosine diphosphate (ADP), respectively, all are diagnostic fragments of the ADPR moiety (Figure 3B; Rosenthal et al., 2015). We also detected a series of fragments containing the conversion of arginine to ornithine residues (–42 Da), which is also diagnostic tandem mass fragment of ADP-ribosylated arginine residues (Gehrig et al., 2021). Thus, Ceg3 modifies ANT1 by mono-ADP-ribosylation on residue Arg236.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3B and citations to Rosenthal et al., 2015 and Gehrig et al., 2021.

claim: The modified site Arg236 in ANT1 resides in the end of the fifth transmembrane region.
source: In ANT1, the modified site Arg236 resides in the end of the fifth transmembrane region, which is close to the matrix side of the mitochondrion (Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by structural information cited from Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003 and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Only mutations in Arg236 abolished Ceg3-induced ADP-ribosylation of ANT1.
source: Only mutations in Arg236 abolished Ceg3-induced ADP-ribosylation (Figure 3D). These results establish that Ceg3 specifically modifies Arg236 in the conserved -R235RRMMM240 motif in ANT1.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Yeast ADP/ATP carriers are targeted by Ceg3 for ADP-ribosylation modification.
source: Although the expression of His6-Ceg3 in yeast cells was not detectable with a His6-specific antibody, ADP-ribosylation of proteins with a molecular weight close to those of ADP/ATP carriers was detected in lysates of yeast cells expressing Ceg3 but not Ceg3E/A (Figure 3E). Thus, yeast ADP/ATP carriers are also targeted by Ceg3 for ADP-ribosylation modification, which likely accounts for its toxicity.
evidence: This is supported by yeast expression and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Ceg3 can modify ANT1 when co-expressed in E. coli.
source: Importantly, when co-expressed in E. coli, Ceg3-induced ANT1 modification was detectable, again in a manner that requires the mART motif (Figure 3—figure supplement 4B). The ability of Ceg3 to modify ANT1 in E. coli indicates that this enzyme functions without the need of co-factors from eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is supported by E. coli co-expression data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4B.

claim: ADP-ribosylation of ANTs is detectable in cells infected with L. pneumophila strains expressing Ceg3.
source: It was clearly detectable in samples infected with a strain that lacks the chromosomal ceg3 but expresses the gene from a multicopy plasmid (Figure 4A). ANTs modification was also detected in cells infected with the wild-type strain harboring the plasmid but not in a mutant defective in the Dot/Icm transporter (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by infection and immunoblotting data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: ADP-ribosylation of ANTs induced by wild-type L. pneumophila becomes detectable at 6 hr after bacterial uptake and peaks at 10 hr.
source: Under this experimental condition, ADP-ribosylation of ANTs induced by wild-type L. pneumophila became detectable at 6 hr after bacterial uptake and peaked at 10 hr. Furthermore, the level of modification decreased at 14 hr and was maintained at low level till 18 hr (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is supported by time-course infection data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The ∆ceg3 mutant grew at rates indistinguishable to those of the wild-type strain in BMDMs and Dictyostelium discoideum.
source: Akin to most Dot/Icm substrates that are dispensable for intracellular replication in laboratory infection models, the ∆ceg3 mutant grew at rates indistinguishable to those of the wild-type strain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), indicating that the absence of Ceg3 does not detectably affect the intracellular replication of L. pneumophila in commonly used laboratory hosts.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular replication data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Ceg3 but not Ceg3E/A caused a slight decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: The expression of Ceg3 but not Ceg3E/A caused a slight decrease in MMP. Thus, the impact of Ceg3 on mitochondrial membrane integrity, if any, is moderate.
evidence: This is supported by MMP measurement data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Expression of Ceg3 in HEK293T cells causes a decrease in ADP/ATP exchange.
source: Expression of Ceg3 but not Ceg3E/A in HEK293T cells caused a decrease in ADP/ATP exchange (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by ADP/ATP exchange rate measurements shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Inhibition of ADP/ATP exchange occurs in mitochondria isolated from cells infected with L. pneumophila strains capable of inducing detectable ANT ADP-ribosylation.
source: Moreover, such inhibition also occurred in mitochondria isolated from cells infected with L. pneumophila strains capable of inducing detectable ANT ADP-ribosylation (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by infection and ADP/ATP exchange rate data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Ceg3 did not induce mitophagy in COS-1 cells.
source: Under our experimental conditions in which cells were uniformly transduced and the expression of Ceg3 is readily detectable, the levels of PDHA1 were similar among all samples (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that Ceg3 did not induce mitophagy.
evidence: This is supported by lentiviral transduction and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ceg3 does not suppress or augment CCCP-induced mitophagy.
source: While treatment with this protonophore did lead to a drastic decrease in PDHA1, such decrease did not detectably change between samples expressing Ceg3 or Ceg3E/A (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C). Thus, Ceg3 does not suppress or augment CCCP-induced mitophagy.
evidence: This is supported by CCCP treatment and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: At least 30% of LCVs were surrounded by mitochondria within 15 min of phagocytosis, which increases to approximately 65% at 1 hr.
source: At least 30% of LCVs were surrounded by mitochondria within 15 min of phagocytosis, which increases to approximately 65% when the infection proceeds to 1 hr (Horwitz, 1983).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Horwitz, 1983.

claim: The association of LCV with mitochondria requires the Dot/Icm transporter.
source: This observation was validated by more recent studies, which reveal that such association requires the Dot/Icm transporter essential for L. pneumophila virulence (Tilney et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tilney et al., 2001.

claim: LegS2 contributes to autophagy inhibition by disrupting lipid metabolism in mitochondria.
source: Among these, LegS2, a homolog of the eukaryotic enzyme sphingosine-1-phosphate lyse, contributes to autophagy inhibition by disrupting lipid metabolism in mitochondria (Degtyar et al., 2009; Rolando et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Degtyar et al., 2009 and Rolando et al., 2016.

claim: MitF modulates mitochondrial dynamics by provoking a Warburg-like effect to benefit intracellular bacterial replication.
source: MitF appears to modulate mitochondrial dynamics by provoking a Warburg-like effect to benefit intracellular bacterial replication (Escoll et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Escoll et al., 2017.

claim: The three arginine residues in the -RRRMMM- motif are essential for the transport function of the yeast ADP/ATP carrier Aac2.
source: The three arginine residues in the -RRRMMM- motif are essential for the transport function of the yeast ADP/ATP carrier Aac2 (Müller et al., 1996; Nelson et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Müller et al., 1996 and Nelson et al., 1993.

claim: Mutations in each of the three arginine residues in the -RRRMMM- motif in the bovine ADP/ATP carrier abolish its transport activity.
source: Mutations in each of these three arginine residues in the bovine ADP/ATP carrier abolish its transport activity, so does a mutation in Arg246 (equivalent to Arg236 in mammalian ANT1) of the mitochondrial carrier from Thermothelomyces thermophile (Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003; Ruprecht et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003 and Ruprecht et al., 2019.

claim: The ADP/ATP translocase-associated mitophagy is independent of its nucleotide translocase activity.
source: Moreover, our finding that Ceg3 does not interfere with mitophagy is in line with a previous study showing that the ADP/ATP translocase-associated mitophagy is independent of its nucleotide translocase activity (Hoshino et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hoshino et al., 2019.

claim: The second arginine in the -RRRMMM- element is implicated in ADP binding via electrostatic interactions with the negatively charged phosphate moieties in ADP.
source: Although the positioning of the -RRRMMM- element revealed by these two structural analyses slightly differs, both studies conclude that the second arginine is implicated in ADP binding via its positively charged side chain that mediates electrostatic interactions with the negatively charged phosphate moieties in ADP (Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003; Ruprecht et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003 and Ruprecht et al., 2014.

claim: Ceg3-mediated ADP-ribosylation on ANTs likely affects the electrostatic interactions with ADP.
source: At neutral pH, ADP-ribose harbors two negatively charged phosphate moieties, which can cause a notable change in the charge property of the side chain of this arginine residue (Laing et al., 2011). Thus, Ceg3-mediated ADP-ribosylation on ANTs likely affects the electrostatic interactions with ADP.
evidence: This is inferred from the chemical properties of ADP-ribose and supported by a citation to Laing et al., 2011.

claim: The bulky ADPR moiety on ANTs may cause steric interference for ADP interaction.
source: In addition, the bulky ADPR moiety on ANTs may cause steric interference for the interaction, both of which can contribute to the inhibition of their ADP/ATP exchange ability.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the mechanism of inhibition.

claim: The Dot/Icm effector LncP has been suggested to carry out unidirectional ATP transport across membranes reconstituted in liposomes.
source: The Dot/Icm effector LncP, which is homologous to mitochondrial carrier proteins, has been suggested to carry out unidirectional ATP transport across membranes reconstituted in liposomes (Dolezal et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Dolezal et al., 2012.

claim: Lpg1625 and Lpg0898 are targeting to the mitochondria.
source: An earlier study found that Lpg1625 and Lpg0898 are targeting to this organelle (Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2013.

claim: Lpg2444 protects the integrity of mitochondria by making it resistant to MMP damage caused by protonophores such as CCCP.
source: Lpg2444 was recently shown to protect the integrity of mitochondria by making it resistant to MMP damage caused by protonophores such as CCCP. This protein also interacts with ADP/ATP translocase 2, but the biological significance of such interactions remains elusive (Noack et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Noack et al., 2020.

claim: None of the mitochondria-targeting effectors harbor a discernable canonical mitochondrial localization signal (MLS) or mitochondrial targeting sequence (MTS).
source: Intriguingly, although these effectors clearly are targeted to the mitochondria, none of them harbors a discernable canonical mitochondrial localization signal (MLS) or mitochondrial targeting sequence (MTS) found in eukaryotic proteins (Habib et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Habib et al., 2007.

claim: The key residues in the predicted mART of Ceg3 are identical to those of bacterial toxins or effector proteins, including ExoS, CtxA, and members of the SidE family.
source: The key residues in the predicted mART of Ceg3 are identical to those of bacterial toxins or effector proteins, including ExoS of P. aeruginosa (Vareechon et al., 2017), CtxA of Vibrio cholera (Cassel and Pfeuffer, 1978), and members of the SidE family of L. pneumophila (Qiu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1A and citations.

claim: The sequence of the predicted mART in Ceg3 is R44-S94-E141KE143.
source: The sequence of the predicted mART in Ceg3 is R44-S94-E141KE143, which resides in its central region (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 1A.

claim: Ceg3 does not co-fractionate with Calnexin or GM130, markers for the ER and the Golgi apparatus.
source: In agreement with results from immunostaining experiments, Flag-Ceg3 did not co-fractionate with Calnexin or GM130, markers for the ER and the Golgi apparatus.
evidence: This is supported by cell fractionation data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Flag-MavC co-fractionated with the cytosolic protein tubulin.
source: In contrast, Flag-MavC co-fractionated with the cytosolic protein tubulin (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by cell fractionation data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Cytochrome c and ATPB can be stripped from mitochondria by high pH buffer.
source: Two peripheral membrane proteins, cytochrome c (Cyto-C) and the beta subunit of ATP synthase (ATPB) that are associated with inner mitochondrial membranes (Walker and Dickson, 2006; Garrido et al., 2006), can be stripped from the mitochondria effectively by the high pH buffer (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is supported by carbonate extraction data shown in Figure 1G and citations to Walker and Dickson, 2006 and Garrido et al., 2006.

claim: The protein detected by the ADP-ribose antibody in Ceg3-expressing cells was not self-modified Flag-Ceg3.
source: Probing these samples with antibodies specific for Flag and ADP-ribose simultaneously detected two proteins of distinct sizes in samples expressing Flag-Ceg3, indicating that the protein detected by the ADP-ribose antibody was not self-modified Flag-Ceg3 (Figure 2A, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by dual immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Af1521 is a protein from Archaeoglobus fulgidus that contains a macro domain involved in binding ADP-ribose moieties on modified proteins.
source: To identify the substrates modified by Ceg3, we enriched ADP-ribosylated proteins from samples of cells transfected to express this effector by using recombinant Af1521, a protein from Archaeoglobus fulgidus that contains a macro domain involved in binding ADP-ribose moieties on modified proteins (Allen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Allen et al., 2003.

claim: S. cerevisiae expresses three ADP/ATP carrier isoforms: Aac1p, Aac2p, and Aac3p.
source: ADP/ATP carriers are evolutionarily conserved in eukaryotes, which in S. cerevisiae are represented by three isoforms, Aac1p, Aac2p, and Aac3p. These proteins have molecular weights similar to those of their mammalian counterparts and each harbors the -RRRMMM- element (Ruprecht et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ruprecht et al., 2014.

claim: Ceg3 functions without the need of co-factors from eukaryotic cells.
source: The ability of Ceg3 to modify ANT1 in E. coli indicates that this enzyme functions without the need of co-factors from eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ceg3 can modify ANT1 when co-expressed in E. coli.

claim: L. pneumophila temporally regulates ANTs by ADP-ribosylation.
source: This modification pattern suggests that L. pneumophila temporally regulates ANTs by ADP-ribosylation either by differently controlling the expression of Ceg3 at different phases of infection or by injecting enzymes capable of reversing the modification at infection phases beyond 10 hr.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal pattern of ANT modification observed in Figure 4C.

claim: The absence of Ceg3 does not detectably affect the intracellular replication of L. pneumophila in commonly used laboratory hosts.
source: Akin to most Dot/Icm substrates that are dispensable for intracellular replication in laboratory infection models, the ∆ceg3 mutant grew at rates indistinguishable to those of the wild-type strain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), indicating that the absence of Ceg3 does not detectably affect the intracellular replication of L. pneumophila in commonly used laboratory hosts.
evidence: This is supported by intracellular replication data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: ATP production entirely depends on the integrity of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP).
source: The main role of mitochondrion is ATP production and regulation of metabolism flux, and the production of ATP entirely depends on the integrity of mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) (Zorova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zorova et al., 2018.

claim: CCCP damages the MMP by uncoupling the proton gradient.
source: As expected, treatment with the ionophore carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenyl hydrazine (CCCP) that damages the MMP by uncoupling the proton gradient, rendered the cells to emit green fluorescence signals (Figure 5A; Georgakopoulos et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by MMP measurement data shown in Figure 5A and a citation to Georgakopoulos et al., 2017.

claim: ATP is transported across the inner mitochondrial membrane by ANTs via exchange with ADP at a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: ATP is transported across the inner mitochondrial membrane by ANTs via exchange with ADP at a 1:1 stoichiometry (Pfaff et al., 1965)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pfaff et al., 1965.

claim: ANT1 is critical for the induction of mitophagy.
source: A recent study showed that ANT1 is critical for the induction of mitophagy (Hoshino et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hoshino et al., 2019.

claim: COS-1 cells undergo robust mitophagy upon being treated with CCCP.
source: After testing a few cell lines, we found that COS-1 cells undergo robust mitophagy upon being treated with the protonophores CCCP, which caused a clear loss of two mitochondrial proteins, PDHA1 and ATPB (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by CCCP treatment and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Transduction of COS-1 cells with lentiviral particles expressing Ceg3 led to mART-dependent ADP-ribosylation of endogenous ANTs.
source: Transduction of COS-1 cells with our lentiviral particles led to mART-dependent ADP-ribosylation of endogenous ANTs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by lentiviral transduction and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mitochondrion is involved in diverse functions such as cell death, immunity, and metabolism regulation.
source: In addition to powering most cellular activities by ATP production, mitochondria are involved in diverse functions such as cell death, immunity, and metabolism regulation (McBride et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to McBride et al., 2006.

claim: Mitochondria are a common target for infectious agents.
source: As a result, this organelle is a common target for infectious agents that actively manipulate host cellular processes for their survival and replication (Lobet et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lobet et al., 2015.

claim: The V. cholera T3SS effector VopE inhibits the activity of Miro1 and Miro2 by functioning as a GTPase-activating protein (GAP).
source: For example, the V. cholera T3SS effector VopE inhibits the activity of Miro1 and Miro2, two mitochondrial GTPases, by functioning as a GTPase-activating protein (GAP), thus suppressing host innate immune responses (Suzuki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Suzuki et al., 2014.

claim: The effector ECH0825 from Ehrlichia chaffeensis upregulates the mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase to prevent ROS-induced cellular damage and mitochondria-mediated apoptosis.
source: The effector ECH0825 from Ehrlichia chaffeensis upregulates the mitochondrial manganese superoxide dismutase to prevent ROS-induced cellular damage and mitochondria-mediated apoptosis (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2012.

claim: The bacterium can gain better control of ATP transport in the mitochondria if it uses one set of effectors to inhibit the endogenous carriers and another set to substitute this function.
source: Although the possibility that Ceg3 coordinates its activity with LncP in L. pneumophila infected cells needs further investigation, it is conceivable that the bacterium can gain better control of ATP transport in the mitochondria if it uses one set of effectors to inhibit the endogenous carriers and another set to substitute this function.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about bacterial strategy.

claim: The -RRRMMM- element is in close proximity to the mitochondrial matrix in the bovine ADP/ATP carrier structure.
source: Structure of the bovine ADP/ATP carrier shows that Arg236 of ANT1 is localized in the end of the fifth transmembrane helix, which is in close proximity to the mitochondrial matrix (Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pebay-Peyroula et al., 2003.

claim: In the Aac2 carrier from yeast, the -RRRMMM- element appears to be in the mitochondrial matrix.
source: In the Aac2 carrier from yeast, the -RRRMMM- element appears to be in the mitochondrial matrix (Ruprecht et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ruprecht et al., 2014.
